title: Amazon behavioral round: Leadership Principles deep dive
inspired_by: Amazon interviewers spend much of every round on the 16 Leadership Principles and probe each story with several follow-ups. This round practices only that: four principles per session, drawn from a bank of 32 original questions. An original simulation, not real Amazon questions.
summary: Four Leadership Principles questions, a different mix every session, each with three probing follow-ups, then your questions for the interviewer. Graded story by story on STAR, ownership, impact, follow-ups, and self-awareness.

cues.amz_intro: Hi, thanks for joining. I'm an engineer here, and today is all about your past experience. I'll ask about four situations, with follow-ups on each. Use real, specific examples, and tell me what you personally did. To start, tell me a little about yourself.
cues.amz_wrap: That's all the questions I have. What questions do you have for me?

followups.leadership: Map your best eight stories to the 16 principles in a table (one story can cover two or three). Fill any principle with no story before your next session.
followups.star: Rewrite your weakest story as four labeled lines (Situation, Task, Action, Result), then say it aloud in under 2.5 minutes.
followups.impact: For each story, find one number for the result (time saved, users, percent, grade) and rewrite every “we” as what you did.
followups.followups: For each story, write the answers to: What did you do yourself? How did you measure it? What would you do differently? Then practice with this round again.
followups.self_awareness: Prepare two stories about real mistakes or failures, each ending with what you changed afterwards.
followups.communication: Time yourself telling three stories; aim for 2–3 minutes each, and prepare three questions about the team to ask at the end.
